name: Refinery flue gas and FCC carbon capture
principle: CO2 is captured from refinery combustion and FCC regenerator flue gas, usually with amine absorption, then compressed for storage. IEA lists post-combustion and oxy-fuel capture for cracking units at TRL 5. In the Netherlands the Porthos system will carry CO2 from Shell's Pernis refinery and three other industrial customers to depleted gas fields.

performance.basis: 37 Mt over 15 years; compressed from 35 bar up to 130 bar; stored about 3 km below the sea surface in depleted fields P18-2, P18-4, P18-6

source.note: iO+, The first Dutch carbon capture and storage plant is taking shape (Porthos)

reference_plants.name: Porthos CO2 transport and storage, Rotterdam (Pernis refinery is a source)
reference_plants.status: works from 2024, operational expected 2026 per the article

source.note: iO+, The first Dutch carbon capture and storage plant is taking shape (Porthos)

limitations: The source describes transport and storage, not the capture unit at the refinery
